scope: Leviticus 23–25, all 122 public verses. Prior revisions remain unchanged.

source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public and Hebrew numbering align throughout Leviticus 23–25. The exact original XML records include all five source annotations, including the written not and read has a wall at 25:30; no numbering shift occurs in this batch.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial assessments are separate from similarity scores. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Keeps the new divine speech boundary and named recipient in a short narrative clause.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses,
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Retains the shift from the LORD’s to my and the repeated appointed-times frame rather than removing it as redundant.
verses.before: “Speak to the Israelites and say to them: The LORD’s appointed times, which you will proclaim as holy assemblies—these are my appointed times.
verses.after: “Tell the Israelites: These are the LORD’s appointed times, which you are to announce as sacred assemblies. These are my appointed times.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Speak to the Israelites and say to them: The LORD’s appointed times, which you shall proclaim as holy assemblies—these are my appointed times.

verses.rationale: Separates the six-day permission from the seventh-day prohibition and preserves the unrestricted no-work wording.
verses.before: Six days work may be done, but the seventh day is a Sabbath of complete rest, a holy assembly. You will do no work. It is a Sabbath to the LORD in all your dwellings.
verses.after: You may work for six days. The seventh day is a Sabbath of complete rest, a sacred assembly. Do no work at all. It is a Sabbath to the LORD wherever you live.
verses.tsw_comparator: Six days work may be done, but the seventh day is a Sabbath of complete rest, a holy assembly. You shall do no work. It is a Sabbath to the LORD in all your dwellings.

verses.rationale: Preserves the renewed introduction after the weekly Sabbath and the repeated time language.
verses.before: These are the appointed times of the LORD, holy assemblies that you will proclaim at their appointed times.
verses.after: These are the LORD’s appointed times, the sacred assemblies you are to announce at their appointed times.
verses.tsw_comparator: These are the appointed times of the LORD, holy assemblies that you shall proclaim at their appointed times.

verses.rationale: Retains the exact date and Passover name; twilight renders between the evenings with its timing uncertainty noted.
verses.before: In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month at twilight, is the LORD’s Passover.
verses.after: In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month at twilight, comes the LORD’s Passover.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month at twilight, is the LORD’s Passover.

verses.rationale: Makes the following date and seven-day practice easy to follow without merging Passover and Unleavened Bread.
verses.before: On the fifteenth day of the same month is the Festival of Unleavened Bread to the LORD. Seven days you will eat unleavened bread.
verses.after: On the fifteenth day of that month comes the LORD’s Festival of Unleavened Bread. Eat unleavened bread for seven days.
verses.tsw_comparator: On the fifteenth day of the same month is the Festival of Unleavened Bread to the LORD. Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes work of service from the broader no-work prohibition in verse 3.
verses.before: On the first day you will have a holy assembly; you will do no regular work.
verses.after: Hold a sacred assembly on the first day. Do none of your ordinary work.
verses.tsw_comparator: On the first day you shall have a holy assembly; you shall do no regular work.

verses.rationale: Preserves all seven offering days and the seventh-day assembly, with a complete closing speech boundary.
verses.before: Seven days you will bring an offering by fire to the LORD. On the seventh day there will be a holy assembly; you will do no regular work.”
verses.after: For seven days, bring offerings by fire to the LORD. On the seventh day, hold a sacred assembly and do none of your ordinary work.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Seven days you shall bring an offering by fire to the LORD. On the seventh day there shall be a holy assembly; you shall do no regular work.”

verses.rationale: Retains the second divine instruction rather than making all calendar material one uninterrupted speech.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses,
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Preserves land as divine gift and the initial harvest presentation; sheaf is the selected sense of omer, noted against a measured grain portion.
verses.before: “Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When you come into the land that I am giving you and reap its harvest, you will bring the first sheaf of your harvest to the priest.
verses.after: “Tell the Israelites: When you enter the land I am giving you and harvest its crops, bring the priest a sheaf from the first of your harvest.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When you come into the land that I am giving you and reap its harvest, you shall bring the first sheaf of your harvest to the priest.

verses.rationale: Keeps both wave actions, acceptance for the people, and the unresolved calendar reference to the Sabbath.
verses.before: He will elevate the sheaf before the LORD so that you may be accepted. On the day after the Sabbath the priest will elevate it.
verses.after: The priest is to wave the sheaf before the LORD so it will be accepted on your behalf. He is to wave it on the day after the Sabbath.
verses.tsw_comparator: He shall elevate the sheaf before the LORD so that you may be accepted. On the day after the Sabbath the priest shall elevate it.

verses.rationale: Preserves age, sex, condition, timing and offering category; lamb’s masculine designation is not generalized away.
verses.before: On the day you elevate the sheaf, you will bring a male lamb a year old without defect as a burnt offering to the LORD.
verses.after: On the day you wave the sheaf, offer the LORD a year-old male lamb without blemish as a burnt offering.
verses.tsw_comparator: On the day you elevate the sheaf, you shall bring a male lamb a year old without defect as a burnt offering to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps the distinct dry and liquid measures, oil mixture and aroma formula; supplied ephah makes the tenth-unit intelligible.
verses.before: Its grain offering will be two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil, an offering by fire to the LORD, a pleasing aroma; and its drink offering will be one-fourth of a hin of wine.
verses.after: Its grain offering is to be two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil, an offering by fire to the LORD, a pleasing aroma. Its drink offering is to be a quarter of a hin of wine.
verses.tsw_comparator: Its grain offering shall be two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil, an offering by fire to the LORD, a pleasing aroma; and its drink offering shall be one-fourth of a hin of wine.

verses.rationale: Retains all three prohibited foods and the offering as the boundary of the prohibition, not simply sunrise on a date.
verses.before: You will eat no bread, roasted grain, or fresh grain until that very day, until you have brought the offering of your God. It is a perpetual statute throughout your generations in all your dwellings.
verses.after: Eat no bread, roasted grain or fresh grain until that very day, when you bring your God’s offering. This is a lasting rule for your generations, wherever you live.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall eat no bread, roasted grain, or fresh grain until that very day, until you have brought the offering of your God. It is a perpetual statute throughout your generations in all your dwellings.

verses.rationale: Retains Hebrew Sabbaths while unfolding the complete-period requirement in readable English; note preserves calendar disagreement.
verses.before: You will count from the day after the Sabbath, from the day you brought the sheaf of the elevation offering: seven complete Sabbaths.
verses.after: Starting with the day after the Sabbath, the day you bring the sheaf as a wave offering, count seven Sabbaths. The count must cover seven full weeks.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall count from the day after the Sabbath, from the day you brought the sheaf of the elevation offering: seven complete Sabbaths.

verses.rationale: Keeps both fifty-day count and seventh-Sabbath endpoint rather than replacing either with a later festival date.
verses.before: You will count fifty days to the day after the seventh Sabbath, and then bring a new grain offering to the LORD.
verses.after: Count fifty days, up to the day after the seventh Sabbath. Then bring the LORD an offering of new grain.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall count fifty days to the day after the seventh Sabbath, and then bring a new grain offering to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves two discrete breads and the deliberately leavened preparation; the quantity is not incorrectly assigned to each loaf.
verses.before: From your dwellings you will bring two loaves as an elevation offering, made from two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour and baked with yeast, as first produce to the LORD.
verses.after: Bring two loaves from where you live as a wave offering. Make them with two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour and bake them with leaven, as firstfruits for the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: From your dwellings you shall bring two loaves as an elevation offering, made from two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour and baked with yeast, as first produce to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains all three animal groups, exact numbers and male lambs, and accompanying offerings rather than compressing the list.
verses.before: With the bread you will bring seven male lambs a year old without defect, one young bull, and two rams. They will be a burnt offering to the LORD with their grain offering and drink offerings, an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
verses.after: With the bread, bring seven year-old male lambs without blemish, one young bull and two rams. They are to be a burnt offering to the LORD, with their grain offering and drink offerings—an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: With the bread you shall bring seven male lambs a year old without defect, one young bull, and two rams. They shall be a burnt offering to the LORD with their grain offering and drink offerings, an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps sin and peace offerings separate from the preceding burnt offering and preserves the goat’s sex and the lambs’ age and sex.
verses.before: You will also prepare one male goat as a sin offering and two male lambs a year old as a sacrifice of well-being.
verses.after: Offer one male goat as a sin offering and two year-old male lambs as a peace sacrifice.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall also prepare one male goat as a sin offering and two male lambs a year old as a sacrifice of well-being.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated two-lamb phrase and pronoun without inventing a physical waving procedure or silently resolving every referent.
verses.before: The priest will elevate them with the bread of the first produce as an elevation offering before the LORD, together with the two lambs. They will be holy to the LORD for the priest.
verses.after: The priest is to wave them before the LORD with the firstfruits bread, together with the two lambs, as a wave offering. They are holy to the LORD and belong to the priest.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest shall elevate them with the bread of the first produce as an elevation offering before the LORD, together with the two lambs. They shall be holy to the LORD for the priest.

verses.rationale: Preserves emphatic same-day timing, ordinary-work restriction and intergenerational geographic scope.
verses.before: On that same day you will proclaim a holy assembly. You will do no regular work. It is a perpetual statute in all your dwellings throughout your generations.
verses.after: On that very day, announce a sacred assembly for yourselves. Do none of your ordinary work. This is a lasting rule for your generations, wherever you live.
verses.tsw_comparator: On that same day you shall proclaim a holy assembly. You shall do no regular work. It is a perpetual statute in all your dwellings throughout your generations.

verses.rationale: Echoes the already revised 19:9–10 gleaning language because the source repeats it; retains both beneficiary groups.
verses.before: When you reap the harvest of your land, you will not reap your field all the way to its edge, and you will not gather the gleanings of your harvest. You will leave them for the poor and for the resident alien. I am the LORD your God.”
verses.after: When you harvest your land, do not reap right to the edges of your field or gather what the harvesters leave behind. Leave it for the poor and the foreigner living among you. I am the LORD your God.”
verses.tsw_comparator: When you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not reap your field all the way to its edge, and you shall not gather the gleanings of your harvest. You shall leave them for the poor and for the resident alien. I am the LORD your God.”

verses.rationale: Marks the new seventh-month instruction as a separate divine speech.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses,
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Preserves remembrance and teruah without inserting a named trumpet or shofar that this verse does not specify.
verses.before: “Speak to the Israelites, saying: In the seventh month, on the first day of the month, you will have a complete rest, a memorial proclaimed with trumpet blasts, a holy assembly.
verses.after: “Tell the Israelites: On the first day of the seventh month, you are to rest and hold a sacred assembly, a remembrance marked by blasts of sound.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Speak to the Israelites, saying: In the seventh month, on the first day of the month, you shall have a complete rest, a memorial proclaimed with trumpet blasts, a holy assembly.

verses.rationale: Retains both the ordinary-work ban and the positive offering instruction.
verses.before: You will do no regular work, and you will bring an offering by fire to the LORD.”
verses.after: Do none of your ordinary work, and bring an offering by fire to the LORD.”
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall do no regular work, and you shall bring an offering by fire to the LORD.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the Day of Atonement speech boundary.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses,
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Keeps the date and established deny-yourselves idiom rather than reducing the Hebrew to an explicit fasting rule.
verses.before: “Now on the tenth day of this seventh month is the Day of Atonement. It will be a holy assembly for you; you will humble yourselves and bring an offering by fire to the LORD.
verses.after: “The tenth day of this seventh month is the Day of Atonement. Hold a sacred assembly, deny yourselves and bring an offering by fire to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Now on the tenth day of this seventh month is the Day of Atonement. It shall be a holy assembly for you; you shall humble yourselves and bring an offering by fire to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains the broader work ban and repeated atonement purpose, avoiding an ordinary-work limitation.
verses.before: You will do no work on that very day, for it is the Day of Atonement, to make atonement for you before the LORD your God.
verses.after: Do no work at all on that very day. It is a day of atonement, when atonement is made for you before the LORD your God.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall do no work on that very day, for it is the Day of Atonement, to make atonement for you before the LORD your God.

verses.rationale: Preserves cut-off language without assigning its mechanism, and keeps the self-denial condition distinct from work.
verses.before: Anyone who does not humble themselves on that very day will be cut off from the people.
verses.after: Anyone who does not deny themselves on that very day will be cut off from their people.
verses.tsw_comparator: Anyone who does not humble themselves on that very day shall be cut off from the people.

verses.rationale: Makes the divine first-person agent explicit and preserves destroy as distinct from the preceding passive cut off.
verses.before: Anyone who does any work on that very day, I will destroy that person from among the people.
verses.after: And anyone who does any work on that very day—I will destroy that person from among their people.
verses.tsw_comparator: Anyone who does any work on that very day, I will destroy that person from among the people.

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated comprehensive work prohibition and its continuing scope.
verses.before: You will do no work. It is a perpetual statute throughout your generations in all your dwellings.
verses.after: Do no work at all. This is a lasting rule for your generations, wherever you live.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall do no work. It is a perpetual statute throughout your generations in all your dwellings.

verses.rationale: Unfolds evening-to-evening timing while preserving the ninth-evening start and tenth-day designation in verse 27.
verses.before: It will be a Sabbath of complete rest for you, and you will humble yourselves. On the ninth day of the month at evening, from evening to evening, you will keep your Sabbath.”
verses.after: It is a Sabbath of complete rest for you, and you must deny yourselves. Observe your Sabbath from the evening of the ninth day of the month until the next evening.”
verses.tsw_comparator: It shall be a Sabbath of complete rest for you, and you shall humble yourselves. On the ninth day of the month at evening, from evening to evening, you shall keep your Sabbath.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the final calendar speech introduction.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses,
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Keeps booths as the biblical festival name and preserves its date and duration.
verses.before: “Speak to the Israelites, saying: On the fifteenth day of this seventh month is the Festival of Booths for seven days to the LORD.
verses.after: “Tell the Israelites: Starting on the fifteenth day of this seventh month, celebrate the Festival of Booths to the LORD for seven days.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Speak to the Israelites, saying: On the fifteenth day of this seventh month is the Festival of Booths for seven days to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps the first-day assembly and the narrower ordinary-work wording.
verses.before: On the first day there will be a holy assembly; you will do no regular work.
verses.after: Hold a sacred assembly on the first day. Do none of your ordinary work.
verses.tsw_comparator: On the first day there shall be a holy assembly; you shall do no regular work.

verses.rationale: Preserves the eighth-day gathering in addition to the seven festival days and retains atseret without assuming a modern observance.
verses.before: Seven days you will bring an offering by fire to the LORD. On the eighth day you will have a holy assembly and bring an offering by fire to the LORD. It is a solemn assembly; you will do no regular work.
verses.after: For seven days, bring offerings by fire to the LORD. On the eighth day, hold a sacred assembly and bring an offering by fire to the LORD. It is a solemn gathering; do none of your ordinary work.
verses.tsw_comparator: Seven days you shall bring an offering by fire to the LORD. On the eighth day you shall have a holy assembly and bring an offering by fire to the LORD. It is a solemn assembly; you shall do no regular work.

verses.rationale: Keeps all four categories and the day-by-day allocation as the summary returns to appointed times.
verses.before: These are the LORD’s appointed times, which you will proclaim as holy assemblies, to bring offerings by fire to the LORD—burnt offering, grain offering, sacrifice, and drink offerings, each on its appointed day—
verses.after: These are the LORD’s appointed times, which you are to announce as sacred assemblies. Bring offerings by fire to the LORD: burnt offerings, grain offerings, sacrifices and drink offerings, each on its proper day.
verses.tsw_comparator: These are the LORD’s appointed times, which you shall proclaim as holy assemblies, to bring offerings by fire to the LORD—burnt offering, grain offering, sacrifice, and drink offerings, each on its appointed day—

verses.rationale: Retains the fourfold besides construction so calendar offerings do not appear to replace other obligations or gifts.
verses.before: besides the LORD’s Sabbaths, besides your gifts, besides all your vow offerings, and besides all your freewill offerings that you give to the LORD.
verses.after: These are in addition to the LORD’s Sabbaths, in addition to your gifts, in addition to all your vow offerings, and in addition to all your freewill offerings that you give the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: besides the LORD’s Sabbaths, besides your gifts, besides all your vow offerings, and besides all your freewill offerings that you give to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves the renewed harvest setting, repeated date and seven-day duration together with first- and eighth-day rest.
verses.before: On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, when you have gathered in the produce of the land, you will celebrate the LORD’s festival seven days. On the first day there will be complete rest, and on the eighth day complete rest.
verses.after: On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, after you gather the land’s produce, celebrate the LORD’s festival for seven days. The first day is a day of rest, and so is the eighth.
verses.tsw_comparator: On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, when you have gathered in the produce of the land, you shall celebrate the LORD’s festival seven days. On the first day there shall be complete rest, and on the eighth day complete rest.

verses.rationale: Retains fruit as written rather than replacing it with branches; does not specify citron or myrtle or turn the list into booth-building instructions.
verses.before: On the first day you will take fruit from majestic trees, palm branches, branches of leafy trees, and willows of the brook, and you will rejoice before the LORD your God seven days.
verses.after: On the first day, take fruit from splendid trees, palm fronds, branches of leafy trees and willows from the streams. Rejoice before the LORD your God for seven days.
verses.tsw_comparator: On the first day you shall take fruit from majestic trees, palm branches, branches of leafy trees, and willows of the brook, and you shall rejoice before the LORD your God seven days.

verses.rationale: Keeps annual repetition, duration, lasting status and repeated month instead of trimming the ritual cadence.
verses.before: You will celebrate it as a festival to the LORD seven days each year. It is a perpetual statute throughout your generations; you will celebrate it in the seventh month.
verses.after: Celebrate this festival to the LORD for seven days each year. It is a lasting rule for your generations. Celebrate it in the seventh month.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall celebrate it as a festival to the LORD seven days each year. It is a perpetual statute throughout your generations; you shall celebrate it in the seventh month.

verses.rationale: Preserves native-born scope rather than adding resident foreigners; sentence continues across the verse label into its purpose.
verses.before: You will live in booths seven days. Every native-born Israelite will live in booths,
verses.after: Live in booths for seven days. Everyone native-born in Israel is to live in booths,
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall live in booths seven days. Every native-born Israelite shall live in booths,

verses.rationale: Connects the dwelling command to intergenerational knowledge and the exodus without adding a lesson beyond the stated purpose.
verses.before: so that your generations may know that I made the Israelites live in booths when I brought them out of the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.”
verses.after: so your generations will know that I made the Israelites live in booths when I brought them out of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.”
verses.tsw_comparator: so that your generations may know that I made the Israelites live in booths when I brought them out of the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.”

verses.rationale: Closes the chapter with Moses transmitting the appointed times, retaining the opening keyword.
verses.before: So Moses declared to the Israelites the appointed times of the LORD.
verses.after: Moses told the Israelites about the LORD’s appointed times.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Moses declared to the Israelites the appointed times of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains the divine speech boundary before the sanctuary provisions.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses,
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Preserves beaten-olive preparation and regular tending; evening-to-morning timing in the next verse qualifies continually.
verses.before: “Command the Israelites to bring you pure oil of beaten olives for the light, to keep a lamp burning continually.
verses.after: “Command the Israelites to bring you pure oil from beaten olives for the light, so the lamp can be kept burning regularly.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Command the Israelites to bring you pure oil of beaten olives for the light, to keep a lamp burning continually.

verses.rationale: Keeps Aaron alone as in the pinned text, the lamp’s location outside the curtain, and the testimony designation.
verses.before: Outside the curtain of the testimony in the Tent of Meeting, Aaron will arrange it from evening until morning before the LORD continually. It is a perpetual statute throughout your generations.
verses.after: Aaron is to tend it before the LORD from evening until morning, outside the curtain of the testimony in the tent of meeting. This is a lasting rule for your generations.
verses.tsw_comparator: Outside the curtain of the testimony in the Tent of Meeting, Aaron shall arrange it from evening until morning before the LORD continually. It is a perpetual statute throughout your generations.

verses.rationale: Preserves pure as the stated adjective without silently inserting gold or making the ritual condition certain.
verses.before: He will arrange the lamps on the pure lampstand before the LORD continually.
verses.after: He is to tend the lamps on the pure lampstand before the LORD regularly.
verses.tsw_comparator: He shall arrange the lamps on the pure lampstand before the LORD continually.

verses.rationale: Keeps twelve and explicitly assigns the two-tenths quantity to each loaf, unlike 23:17.
verses.before: You will take fine flour and bake twelve cakes from it; each cake will be made from two-tenths of an ephah.
verses.after: Take fine flour and bake twelve loaves, using two-tenths of an ephah for each loaf.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall take fine flour and bake twelve cakes from it; each cake shall be made from two-tenths of an ephah.

verses.rationale: Uses arrangement to avoid deciding whether maarakot means rows or stacks, retaining both counts and pure.
verses.before: You will arrange them in two rows, six in a row, on the pure table before the LORD.
verses.after: Set them in two arrangements, six in each, on the pure table before the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall arrange them in two rows, six in a row, on the pure table before the LORD.

verses.rationale: Makes frankincense the memorial portion rather than implying that the priests’ bread is burned; with does not fix its exact placement.
verses.before: You will put pure frankincense on each row, and it will be with the bread as a memorial portion, an offering by fire to the LORD.
verses.after: Put pure frankincense with each arrangement. It will serve as the bread’s memorial portion, an offering by fire to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall put pure frankincense on each row, and it shall be with the bread as a memorial portion, an offering by fire to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains the doubled Sabbath cadence and covenant language while clarifying the actor and bread referent.
verses.before: Every Sabbath day Aaron will arrange it before the LORD continually on behalf of the Israelites, as a perpetual covenant.
verses.after: Sabbath after Sabbath, Aaron is to arrange the bread before the LORD regularly. It comes from the Israelites as an everlasting covenant.
verses.tsw_comparator: Every Sabbath day Aaron shall arrange it before the LORD continually on behalf of the Israelites, as a perpetual covenant.

verses.rationale: Preserves recipients, holy eating location, most-holy classification and lasting priestly due without equating place and food categories.
verses.before: It will belong to Aaron and his sons, and they will eat it in a holy place, for it is most holy to him from the LORD’s offerings by fire, a perpetual statute.
verses.after: The bread belongs to Aaron and his sons. They are to eat it in a holy place, for it is most holy, his lasting share of the LORD’s offerings by fire.”
verses.tsw_comparator: It shall belong to Aaron and his sons, and they shall eat it in a holy place, for it is most holy to him from the LORD’s offerings by fire, a perpetual statute.

verses.rationale: Clarifies the two fighters and the first man’s parentage without inventing the reason he went out or the cause of the fight.
verses.before: The son of an Israelite woman, whose father was an Egyptian man, went out among the Israelites. The son of the Israelite woman and an Israelite man fought in the camp.
verses.after: A man whose mother was an Israelite and whose father was an Egyptian went out among the Israelites. In the camp, he and an Israelite man began fighting.
verses.tsw_comparator: The son of an Israelite woman, whose father was an Egyptian man, went out among the Israelites. The son of the Israelite woman and an Israelite man fought in the camp.

verses.rationale: Preserves Name and the two verbal actions, with a note on naqav’s uncertain force; retains mother, grandfather and tribe.
verses.before: The Israelite woman’s son blasphemed the Name and cursed, and they brought him to Moses. His mother’s name was Shelomith daughter of Dibri, from the tribe of Dan.
verses.after: The Israelite woman’s son spoke the Name in blasphemy and cursed. They brought him to Moses. His mother was Shelomith, daughter of Dibri, from the tribe of Dan.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Israelite woman’s son blasphemed the Name and cursed, and they brought him to Moses. His mother’s name was Shelomith daughter of Dibri, from the tribe of Dan.

verses.rationale: Unfolds the awkward mouth-of-the-LORD clause without implying they had already decided his punishment.
verses.before: They placed him in custody until the LORD’s decision should be made clear to them.
verses.after: They kept him in custody until the LORD’s own word would make the decision clear to them.
verses.tsw_comparator: They placed him in custody until the LORD’s decision should be made clear to them.

verses.rationale: Keeps the divine ruling separate from the preceding custodial action.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses,
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Preserves the hearers’ participation and the whole assembly’s execution, without inventing a symbolic explanation for the hand-laying.
verses.before: “Bring the one who cursed outside the camp. Everyone who heard him will lay their hands on his head, and the whole congregation will stone him.
verses.after: “Take the man who cursed outside the camp. Everyone who heard him is to lay their hands on his head. Then the whole assembly is to stone him.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Bring the one who cursed outside the camp. All who heard him shall lay their hands on his head, and the whole congregation shall stone him.

verses.rationale: Retains the possessive his God and guilt-bearing language, with a note on the possible broader divine reference.
verses.before: Speak to the Israelites, saying: Anyone who curses his God will bear his sin.
verses.after: Tell the Israelites: Anyone who curses his God will bear the guilt of his sin.
verses.tsw_comparator: Speak to the Israelites, saying: Anyone who curses his God shall bear his sin.

verses.rationale: Keeps both death declarations, communal stoning and equal application to foreigner and native-born; does not broaden this into every legal status.
verses.before: Whoever blasphemes the name of the LORD will surely be put to death; the whole congregation will surely stone that person. The resident alien as well as the native-born will be put to death when blaspheming the Name.
verses.after: Anyone who blasphemes the LORD’s name must be put to death. The whole assembly must stone him. Foreigner and native-born alike must be put to death for blaspheming the Name.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever blasphemes the name of the LORD shall surely be put to death; the whole congregation shall surely stone that person. The resident alien as well as the native-born shall be put to death when blaspheming the Name.

verses.rationale: Makes the fatal force of striking a human life explicit rather than prescribing death for any nonfatal blow.
verses.before: Whoever strikes down a human life will surely be put to death.
verses.after: Anyone who strikes a human being dead must be put to death.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever strikes down a human life shall surely be put to death.

verses.rationale: Preserves restitution for the animal and the life-for-life formula without confusing it with the human death penalty.
verses.before: Whoever strikes down an animal will make restitution for it, life for life.
verses.after: Anyone who strikes an animal dead must replace it, life for life.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever strikes down an animal shall make restitution for it, life for life.

verses.rationale: Renders inflicted mum as bodily injury here while retaining the reciprocal physical wording without substituting later compensation rules.
verses.before: If someone causes an injury to a neighbor, as that person has done, so it will be done to that person:
verses.after: If someone causes a bodily injury to another person, what he has done must be done to him.
verses.tsw_comparator: If anyone causes an injury to a neighbor, as that person has done, so it shall be done to that person:

verses.rationale: Preserves the three paired injuries and the repeated matching-injury statement, not a generalized fairness maxim.
verses.before: fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth. As the person has caused injury to another, so will it be given to that person.
verses.after: Fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth: the injury he caused another person must be inflicted on him.
verses.tsw_comparator: fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth. As the person has caused injury to another, so shall it be given to that person.

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated contrast between animal restitution and human killing rather than deleting it as redundant.
verses.before: Whoever strikes down an animal will make restitution for it, but whoever strikes down a human being will be put to death.
verses.after: Whoever strikes an animal dead must replace it; whoever strikes a human being dead must be put to death.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever strikes down an animal shall make restitution for it, but whoever strikes down a human being shall be put to death.

verses.rationale: Keeps the single legal standard in this context without importing an assertion that all distinctions elsewhere are abolished.
verses.before: You will have one ordinance for the resident alien and for the native-born, for I am the LORD your God.”
verses.after: You are to have one rule for foreigner and native-born alike. I am the LORD your God.”
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall have one ordinance for the resident alien and for the native-born, for I am the LORD your God.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the actual execution and the closing obedience statement, neither softening the harm nor adding moral commentary.
verses.before: Moses spoke to the Israelites, and they brought the one who had cursed outside the camp and stoned him with stones. The Israelites did as the LORD commanded Moses.
verses.after: Moses told the Israelites, and they took the man who had cursed outside the camp and stoned him. The Israelites did as the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses spoke to the Israelites, and they brought the one who had cursed outside the camp and stoned him with stones. The Israelites did as the LORD commanded Moses.

verses.rationale: Retains the explicit Sinai setting for the land laws.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai, saying,
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses on Mount Sinai,
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai, saying,

verses.rationale: Makes the land itself the subject of Sabbath rest and preserves its status as divine gift.
verses.before: “Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When you come into the land that I am giving you, the land will keep a Sabbath to the LORD.
verses.after: “Tell the Israelites: When you enter the land I am giving you, the land is to keep a Sabbath to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When you come into the land that I am giving you, the land shall keep a Sabbath to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated six-year language and both agricultural tasks.
verses.before: Six years you will sow your field, and six years you will prune your vineyard and gather its produce.
verses.after: For six years, sow your field; for six years, prune your vineyard and gather its produce.
verses.tsw_comparator: Six years you shall sow your field, and six years you shall prune your vineyard and gather its produce.

verses.rationale: Preserves land rest and repeated Sabbath language while keeping sowing and pruning as separate prohibitions.
verses.before: But in the seventh year there will be a Sabbath of complete rest for the land, a Sabbath to the LORD. You will not sow your field or prune your vineyard.
verses.after: But in the seventh year, the land is to have a Sabbath of complete rest, a Sabbath to the LORD. Do not sow your field or prune your vineyard.
verses.tsw_comparator: But in the seventh year there shall be a Sabbath of complete rest for the land, a Sabbath to the LORD. You shall not sow your field or prune your vineyard.

verses.rationale: Retains volunteer growth and untended vine categories; note distinguishes organized harvesting from permitted eating in the following verses.
verses.before: You will not reap what grows by itself from your harvest, and you will not gather the grapes of your untrimmed vine. It will be a year of complete rest for the land.
verses.after: Do not reap what grows on its own after your harvest or gather grapes from your untended vines. The land is to have a year of rest.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not reap what grows by itself from your harvest, and you shall not gather the grapes of your untrimmed vine. It shall be a year of complete rest for the land.

verses.rationale: Preserves the full beneficiary list and explicitly names both sexes of enslaved people rather than hiding them within servants.
verses.before: The Sabbath produce of the land will be food for you—for you, your male and female servants, your hired worker, and the resident alien who lives with you,
verses.after: Whatever the land grows during its Sabbath will be food for you, your male and female slaves, your hired worker and the residents staying with you.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Sabbath produce of the land shall be food for you—for you, your male and female servants, your hired worker, and the resident alien who lives with you,

verses.rationale: Keeps both domestic and wild animals as beneficiaries of the land’s produce.
verses.before: and for your livestock and the wild animals in your land. All its produce will be for food.
verses.after: All its produce will also be food for your livestock and the wild animals in your land.
verses.tsw_comparator: and for your livestock and the wild animals in your land. All its produce shall be for food.

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated sevenfold calculation and explicit total instead of collapsing the calendrical pattern.
verses.before: You will count seven Sabbaths of years, seven times seven years, so that the time of the seven Sabbaths of years amounts to forty-nine years.
verses.after: Count seven Sabbaths of years—seven times seven years—so the seven Sabbaths of years come to forty-nine years.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall count seven Sabbaths of years, seven times seven years, so that the time of the seven Sabbaths of years amounts to forty-nine years.

verses.rationale: Retains both date and named day, both soundings, and the explicit shofar absent from 23:24.
verses.before: Then you will sound a loud blast on the horn in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month. On the Day of Atonement you will sound the horn throughout all your land.
verses.after: Then, on the tenth day of the seventh month, sound the horn loudly. On the Day of Atonement, sound the horn throughout your land.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then you shall sound a loud blast on the horn in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month. On the Day of Atonement you shall sound the horn throughout all your land.

verses.rationale: Preserves fifty, all-inhabitant proclamation, Jubilee and both returns; does not erase later restrictions on the persons released.
verses.before: You will make the fiftieth year holy and proclaim liberty throughout the land to all its inhabitants. It will be a Jubilee for you, and each of you will return to your property, and each of you will return to your family.
verses.after: Set the fiftieth year apart as holy and proclaim freedom throughout the land to everyone living in it. It will be a Jubilee for you. Each of you is to return to your family holding, and each of you to your family.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall make the fiftieth year holy and proclaim liberty throughout the land to all its inhabitants. It shall be a Jubilee for you, and each of you shall return to your property, and each of you shall return to your family.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated fiftieth-year designation and all three agricultural restrictions.
verses.before: The fiftieth year will be a Jubilee for you. You will not sow, and you will not reap what grows by itself or gather from the untrimmed vines,
verses.after: The fiftieth year will be a Jubilee for you. Do not sow, reap what grows on its own or gather grapes from the untended vines.
verses.tsw_comparator: The fiftieth year shall be a Jubilee for you. You shall not sow, and you shall not reap what grows by itself or gather from the untrimmed vines,

verses.rationale: Retains holy status and permission to eat field produce alongside the harvesting restrictions.
verses.before: for it is a Jubilee. It will be holy to you. You will eat its produce from the field.
verses.after: It is a Jubilee, holy to you. Eat what the fields produce.
verses.tsw_comparator: for it is a Jubilee. It shall be holy to you. You shall eat its produce from the field.

verses.rationale: Repeats the land-return rule that introduces the valuation and redemption provisions.
verses.before: In this Year of Jubilee each of you will return to your property.
verses.after: In this Jubilee year, each of you is to return to your family holding.
verses.tsw_comparator: In this Year of Jubilee each of you shall return to your property.

verses.rationale: Keeps reciprocal buying and selling and the prohibition of exploitation in understandable commercial language.
verses.before: When you sell something to your neighbor or buy from your neighbor, do not wrong one another.
verses.after: When you sell something to your neighbor or buy from your neighbor, do not cheat one another.
verses.tsw_comparator: When you sell something to your neighbor or buy from your neighbor, do not wrong one another.

verses.rationale: Makes the relationship between Jubilee and remaining crop value explicit while retaining the initial years-since wording.
verses.before: According to the number of years after the Jubilee, you will buy from your neighbor; according to the number of crop years remaining, your neighbor will sell to you.
verses.after: When you buy from your neighbor, base the price on the years since the Jubilee. He is to sell to you according to the number of harvest years left.
verses.tsw_comparator: According to the number of years after the Jubilee, you shall buy from your neighbor; according to the number of crop years remaining, your neighbor shall sell to you.

verses.rationale: Unfolds proportional pricing and preserves the source’s explanation that harvests are being sold.
verses.before: If the years are many, you will increase the price, and if the years are few, you will reduce the price, for what is being sold to you is the number of harvests.
verses.after: More years mean a higher price; fewer years mean a lower price. What he is selling you is a number of harvests.
verses.tsw_comparator: If the years are many, you shall increase the price, and if the years are few, you shall reduce the price, for what is being sold to you is the number of harvests.

verses.rationale: Retains the renewed exploitation prohibition and its stated divine motivation without appending economic commentary.
verses.before: You will not wrong one another, but you will fear your God, for I am the LORD your God.
verses.after: Do not cheat one another. Fear your God, for I am the LORD your God.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not wrong one another, but you shall fear your God, for I am the LORD your God.

verses.rationale: Keeps both legal terms and the link between doing them and secure dwelling.
verses.before: You will do my statutes and keep my ordinances and do them, so that you may dwell securely in the land.
verses.after: Carry out my statutes and keep my ordinances by doing them. Then you will live securely in the land.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall do my statutes and keep my ordinances and do them, so that you may dwell securely in the land.

verses.rationale: Preserves the land’s yield, satisfaction and repeated secure-dwelling promise as three connected clauses.
verses.before: The land will give its fruit, and you will eat your fill and dwell securely in it.
verses.after: The land will yield its produce, you will eat your fill, and you will live there securely.
verses.tsw_comparator: The land will give its fruit, and you will eat your fill and dwell securely in it.

verses.rationale: Gives the anticipated question its own voice and retains both sowing and gathering concerns.
verses.before: If you say, ‘What will we eat in the seventh year, if we do not sow or gather our produce?’
verses.after: You may ask, ‘What will we eat in the seventh year if we do not sow or gather our crops?’
verses.tsw_comparator: If you say, ‘What will we eat in the seventh year, if we do not sow or gather our produce?’

verses.rationale: Preserves the divine first-person promise, sixth-year timing and exact three-year provision.
verses.before: I will command my blessing for you in the sixth year, and it will produce enough for three years.
verses.after: I will command my blessing for you in the sixth year, and it will yield enough produce for three years.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will command my blessing for you in the sixth year, and it will produce enough for three years.

verses.rationale: Retains the difficult sixth/eighth/ninth-year sequence as written rather than adjusting it to an assumed calendar.
verses.before: You will sow in the eighth year, but you will continue eating from the old produce until the ninth year. Until its produce comes in, you will eat from the old.
verses.after: When you sow in the eighth year, you will still be eating the old crop. You will eat from it until the ninth year, until that year’s crop comes in.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will sow in the eighth year, but you will continue eating from the old produce until the ninth year. Until its produce comes in, you will eat from the old.

verses.rationale: Preserves divine ownership and both ger and toshav labels for Israel, connecting land tenure with resident status rather than absolute ownership.
verses.before: The land will not be sold permanently, for the land is mine. You are resident aliens and temporary residents with me.
verses.after: The land must not be sold permanently, because the land is mine. You are foreigners and residents living with me.
verses.tsw_comparator: The land shall not be sold permanently, for the land is mine. You are resident aliens and temporary residents with me.

verses.rationale: Retains the requirement to permit redemption throughout the whole holding, not merely a discretionary purchase option.
verses.before: Throughout all the land of your possession, you will provide for the redemption of the land.
verses.after: Throughout the land you hold, you must allow land to be redeemed.
verses.tsw_comparator: Throughout all the land of your possession, you shall provide for the redemption of the land.

verses.rationale: Keeps kinship language, poverty condition, partial sale and nearest relative’s redemption role.
verses.before: If a fellow Israelite becomes poor and sells some of their property, the nearest redeemer will come and redeem what the relative sold.
verses.after: If your brother becomes poor and sells part of his family holding, his nearest redeemer is to come and redeem what his brother sold.
verses.tsw_comparator: If a fellow Israelite becomes poor and sells some of their property, the nearest redeemer shall come and redeem what the relative sold.

verses.rationale: Unfolds the hand-reaching means idiom and leaves the condition linked to the calculation in the next verse.
verses.before: If someone has no redeemer but later prospers and finds sufficient means to redeem it,
verses.after: If he has no redeemer but later gains enough to redeem it himself,
verses.tsw_comparator: If someone has no redeemer but later prospers and finds sufficient means to redeem it,

verses.rationale: Makes the seller, buyer and balance intelligible while preserving elapsed-year accounting and return.
verses.before: that person will calculate the years since its sale, repay the remaining value to the person to whom it was sold, and return to the property.
verses.after: he is to count the years since the sale and refund the balance to the buyer. Then he may return to his family holding.
verses.tsw_comparator: that person shall calculate the years since its sale, repay the remaining value to the person to whom it was sold, and return to the property.

verses.rationale: Preserves the inability-to-refund condition, buyer’s temporary control and both release and return.
verses.before: But if there are not sufficient means to recover it, what was sold will remain in the hand of the buyer until the Year of Jubilee. In the Jubilee it will be released, and the seller will return to the property.
verses.after: If he cannot afford the refund, what he sold will remain with the buyer until the Jubilee year. At the Jubilee it will be released, and he may return to his family holding.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if there are not sufficient means to recover it, what was sold shall remain in the hand of the buyer until the Year of Jubilee. In the Jubilee it shall be released, and the seller shall return to the property.

verses.rationale: Keeps the full-year window and repeated redemption deadline without confusing a city house with farmland.
verses.before: If someone sells a dwelling house in a walled city, the right of redemption will last until a full year after its sale. The right to redeem it will last one year.
verses.after: If a man sells a house in a walled city, he may redeem it until a full year has passed since the sale. His right to redeem it lasts that year.
verses.tsw_comparator: If someone sells a dwelling house in a walled city, the right of redemption shall last until a full year after its sale. The right to redeem it shall last one year.

verses.rationale: Follows the explicit read form has a wall over written not; preserves permanent tenure, descendants and the Jubilee exception.
verses.before: If it is not redeemed before a full year is complete, the house in the walled city will belong permanently to the buyer throughout the generations. It will not be released in the Jubilee.
verses.after: If it is not redeemed before the full year ends, the house in that walled city becomes the buyer’s permanent property for his generations. It will not be released at the Jubilee.
verses.tsw_comparator: If it is not redeemed before a full year is complete, the house in the walled city shall belong permanently to the buyer throughout the generations. It shall not be released in the Jubilee.

verses.rationale: Preserves the wall-based contrast, field classification and both redemption and Jubilee release.
verses.before: But houses in villages that have no wall around them will be considered as fields of the land. They may be redeemed, and they will be released in the Jubilee.
verses.after: Houses in villages with no surrounding wall are to be treated like open fields. They may be redeemed, and they will be released at the Jubilee.
verses.tsw_comparator: But houses in villages that have no wall around them shall be considered as fields of the land. They may be redeemed, and they shall be released in the Jubilee.

verses.rationale: Retains the permanent redemption right for Levitical houses rather than applying the one-year city-house limit.
verses.before: As for the cities of the Levites, the Levites will always have the right to redeem houses in the cities of their possession.
verses.after: As for the Levites’ cities, the Levites always have the right to redeem houses in the cities they hold.
verses.tsw_comparator: As for the cities of the Levites, the Levites shall always have the right to redeem houses in the cities of their possession.

verses.rationale: Keeps redeem from the Levites as a provisional reading of the difficult opening, notes alternatives, and does not silently insert a negative absent from the pinned text.
verses.before: If one of the Levites does not redeem a sold house, the house in the city of their possession will be released in the Jubilee, for the houses in the cities of the Levites are their possession among the Israelites.
verses.after: If someone redeems a house from the Levites, the house sold in the city they hold is to be released at the Jubilee. The houses in the Levites’ cities are their holding among the Israelites.
verses.tsw_comparator: If one of the Levites does not redeem a sold house, the house in the city of their possession shall be released in the Jubilee, for the houses in the cities of the Levites are their possession among the Israelites.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes unsellable Levitical pastureland from houses that can be sold and redeemed.
verses.before: But the pastureland belonging to their cities will not be sold, for it is their permanent possession.
verses.after: The pastureland around their cities must not be sold, because it is their permanent holding.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the pastureland belonging to their cities shall not be sold, for it is their permanent possession.

verses.rationale: Unfolds failing-hand idiom and selects resident-like support for the brother; note preserves possible inclusion of foreigners as additional beneficiaries.
verses.before: If a fellow Israelite becomes poor and their hand falters beside you, you will support them as you would a resident alien or temporary resident, so that they may live beside you.
verses.after: If your brother becomes poor and cannot support himself among you, support him as you would a foreigner or resident, so he can live with you.
verses.tsw_comparator: If a fellow Israelite becomes poor and their hand falters beside you, you shall support them as you would a resident alien or temporary resident, so that they may live beside you.

verses.rationale: Keeps both Hebrew financial terms and the brother’s continuing livelihood, without narrowing the ban to excessive rates.
verses.before: Do not take interest or profit from them, but fear your God, so that your fellow Israelite may live beside you.
verses.after: Take no interest or increase from him. Fear your God, and let your brother live with you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not take interest or profit from them, but fear your God, so that your fellow Israelite may live beside you.

verses.rationale: Makes the parallel money and food transactions clear without conflating the terms into a single money-loan rule.
verses.before: You will not give your silver to them at interest or give your food for profit.
verses.after: Do not lend him your money at interest or supply him food for a profit.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not give your silver to them at interest or give your food for profit.

verses.rationale: Preserves both purposes of the exodus, land gift and divine relationship, with Canaan named.
verses.before: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan and to be your God.
verses.after: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan and to be your God.
verses.tsw_comparator: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan and to be your God.

verses.rationale: Preserves the sale and the specific ban on slave labor rather than making the transaction ordinary voluntary employment.
verses.before: If a fellow Israelite becomes poor beside you and sells themselves to you, you will not make that person serve as a slave.
verses.after: If your brother becomes poor beside you and is sold to you, do not make him do a slave’s labor.
verses.tsw_comparator: If a fellow Israelite becomes poor beside you and sells themselves to you, you shall not make that person serve as a slave.

verses.rationale: Retains both comparison statuses and the Jubilee endpoint without adding modern contract terms.
verses.before: That person will be with you like a hired worker or temporary resident and will serve with you until the Year of Jubilee.
verses.after: Let him stay with you as a hired worker or resident. He is to work for you until the Jubilee year.
verses.tsw_comparator: That person shall be with you like a hired worker or temporary resident and shall serve with you until the Year of Jubilee.

verses.rationale: Keeps children’s release together with the man and both family and ancestral-land return.
verses.before: Then that person and the children with them will go out from you and return to their family and to the property of their ancestors.
verses.after: Then he and his children are to leave you. He is to return to his family and to his ancestors’ holding.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then that person and the children with them shall go out from you and return to their family and to the property of their ancestors.

verses.rationale: Retains the source’s ownership metaphor using slaves in both halves so the exodus-based contrast remains visible; vocabulary explains the broader eved range.
verses.before: For they are my servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt. They will not be sold as slaves are sold.
verses.after: For they are my slaves, whom I brought out of Egypt. They must not be sold as slaves are sold.
verses.tsw_comparator: For they are my servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt. They shall not be sold as slaves are sold.

verses.rationale: Keeps the ban on harsh mastery and direct divine motivation without inventing a prohibition beyond the stated group.
verses.before: You will not rule over them with harshness, but you will fear your God.
verses.after: Do not rule over him harshly. Fear your God.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not rule over them with harshness, but you shall fear your God.

verses.rationale: Preserves explicit purchase of both sexes from surrounding nations and its repetition, rather than euphemizing slavery as service.
verses.before: As for the male and female slaves you may have, you may acquire male and female slaves from the nations around you.
verses.after: Your male and female slaves may come from the nations around you. From them you may buy male and female slaves.
verses.tsw_comparator: As for the male and female slaves you may have, you may acquire male and female slaves from the nations around you.

verses.rationale: Preserves children of residents, families born in the land and property status; does not turn residence into a guarantee against enslavement.
verses.before: You may also acquire them from the children of the resident aliens who live among you and from their clans who are with you, those born in your land. They may become your property.
verses.after: You may also buy people from among the children of residents staying with you and from their families born in your land. They may become your property.
verses.tsw_comparator: You may also acquire them from the children of the resident aliens who live among you and from their clans who are with you, those born in your land. They may become your property.

verses.rationale: Retains inheritance, permanent enslavement and the explicit Israelite limitation of the harsh-rule prohibition, without smoothing away the unequal treatment.
verses.before: You may leave them as an inheritance to your children after you, to inherit as property. You may have them serve permanently. But over your fellow Israelites you will not rule over one another with harshness.
verses.after: You may pass them on to your sons as inherited property, and you may keep them as slaves permanently. But as for your brothers, the Israelites, none of you is to rule over a brother harshly.
verses.tsw_comparator: You may leave them as an inheritance to your children after you, to inherit as property. You may have them serve permanently. But over your fellow Israelites you shall not rule over one another with harshness.

verses.rationale: Keeps changed economic positions and all purchaser categories; member is provisional for the rare eqer, with descendant/offshoot noted.
verses.before: If a resident alien or temporary resident beside you prospers, and a fellow Israelite beside them becomes poor and sells themselves to the resident alien or temporary resident, or to a member of the resident alien’s clan,
verses.after: If a foreigner or resident living with you becomes wealthy, and your brother becomes poor beside him and is sold to that foreigner or resident, or to a member of the foreigner’s family,
verses.tsw_comparator: If a resident alien or temporary resident beside you prospers, and a fellow Israelite beside them becomes poor and sells themselves to the resident alien or temporary resident, or to a member of the resident alien’s clan,

verses.rationale: Links the right of redemption to the preceding sale and retains a brother’s role.
verses.before: after being sold, that person retains the right of redemption. One of their relatives may redeem them:
verses.after: he retains the right to be redeemed after the sale. One of his brothers may redeem him.
verses.tsw_comparator: after being sold, that person retains the right of redemption. One of their relatives may redeem them:

verses.rationale: Keeps all named kinship options and self-redemption rather than replacing the list with relatives generally.
verses.before: an uncle, an uncle’s child, or another close relative from the clan may redeem them; or if the person prospers, they may redeem themselves.
verses.after: His uncle, his uncle’s son or another close relative from his family may redeem him. Or, if he gains the means, he may redeem himself.
verses.tsw_comparator: an uncle, an uncle’s child, or another close relative from the clan may redeem them; or if the person prospers, they may redeem themselves.

verses.rationale: Preserves joint calculation, original sale-to-Jubilee interval and hired-worker valuation without inventing a wage amount.
verses.before: They will calculate with the buyer from the year they sold themselves until the Year of Jubilee. The price of the sale will correspond to the number of years; the time will be valued like the time of a hired worker.
verses.after: He and his buyer are to count the years from the year he was sold until the Jubilee year. His sale price is to be apportioned by the years, with his time valued like that of a hired worker.
verses.tsw_comparator: They shall calculate with the buyer from the year they sold themselves until the Year of Jubilee. The price of the sale shall correspond to the number of years; the time shall be valued like the time of a hired worker.

verses.rationale: Keeps redemption tied to remaining years and original price rather than accumulated service or a new market price.
verses.before: If many years remain, according to them the person will repay the price of redemption from the purchase price.
verses.after: If many years remain, he is to pay back a share of his purchase price as his redemption payment, in proportion to those years.
verses.tsw_comparator: If many years remain, according to them the person shall repay the price of redemption from the purchase price.

verses.rationale: Retains the few-years counterpart and calculation with the buyer instead of deleting the repeated proportional rule.
verses.before: If only a few years remain until the Year of Jubilee, the person will calculate accordingly; according to the years of service, the person will repay the redemption price.
verses.after: If only a few years remain until the Jubilee, he is to count them with his buyer and pay for his redemption in proportion to those years.
verses.tsw_comparator: If only a few years remain until the Year of Jubilee, the person shall calculate accordingly; according to the years of service, the person shall repay the redemption price.

verses.rationale: Preserves annual hired-worker comparison and the addressed community’s witnessing responsibility implied by before your eyes.
verses.before: The person will be with the buyer like a worker hired year by year. The buyer will not rule with harshness over that person in your sight.
verses.after: He is to be treated as a worker hired year by year. Do not let his buyer rule over him harshly before your eyes.
verses.tsw_comparator: The person shall be with the buyer like a worker hired year by year. The buyer shall not rule with harshness over that person in your sight.

verses.rationale: Keeps failed-redemption condition and release of both the man and his children at Jubilee.
verses.before: If the person is not redeemed by these means, that person and the children with them will go free in the Year of Jubilee.
verses.after: If he is not redeemed in any of these ways, he and his children are to be released in the Jubilee year.
verses.tsw_comparator: If the person is not redeemed by these means, that person and the children with them shall go free in the Year of Jubilee.

verses.rationale: Preserves both statements of divine ownership and the exodus ground with the same slave term as verse 42.
verses.before: For the Israelites are servants to me. They are my servants whom I brought out of the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.
verses.after: For the Israelites are slaves belonging to me. They are my slaves, whom I brought out of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For the Israelites are servants to me. They are my servants whom I brought out of the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.
